extracted.intended_audience: Investigators applying to the FY25 OCRP, peer reviewers, programmatic reviewers, and OCRP program staff
extracted.subtask_description: Description of the CDMRP/OCRP two-tier review process and scoring procedures used to evaluate Investigator-Initiated Research, OCCTA-ECI, and Pilot Award applications for FY25. Covers pre-application screening, peer review panel procedures and scoring, Summary Statements, and programmatic review criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two-tier review requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: An application must be favorably reviewed by both levels of the two-tier review system to be funded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The two-tier model (based on NAS recommendations) combines traditional peer review strengths with program-specific tailoring; favorable outcomes are required at both scientific peer review and programmatic review for funding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-application screening criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Screening followed the pre-application evaluation criteria specified in the program announcements (PAs) to determine which investigators to invite to submit full applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pre-applications were received and screened (June–July) against the PA-specified pre-application evaluation criteria; only invited investigators could submit full applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application compliance with PA requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications must be compliant with PA/application requirements to be considered (the document reports numbers of 'compliant applications received').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Noncompliant applications were not counted among compliant applications; compliance is a gatekeeping criterion during screening and submission assessment (examples in the report show counts of compliant vs. invited).

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer review panel composition and reviewer responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Each peer review panel included a Chair, an average of 10 scientific reviewers, an average of two consumer reviewers, and a nonvoting Scientific Review Officer. Panelists’ primary responsibility was to review the technical merit of each application based upon the evaluation criteria specified in the relevant PA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Panels combine scientific and consumer perspectives; the nonvoting SRO manages the review record and summary statement preparation; reviewers focus on technical merit and apply PA-published criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Individual peer review panel process and deliberation
rubrics_metrics.description: The Chair presided over deliberations, called on assigned reviewers for assessments using the PA evaluation criteria, summarized strengths and weaknesses following discussion, and panel members then rated applications confidentially.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers present assessments, the Chair synthesizes strengths/weaknesses for the record, panel discussion informs reviewers before confidential rating; the process emphasizes assigned-reviewer assessments plus full-panel deliberation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation criteria scores (10–1 whole-number scale)
rubrics_metrics.description: Panel members rated each application based on the peer review evaluation criteria published in the appropriate PA using a scale of 10 to 1, with 10 representing the highest merit and 1 the lowest merit, using whole numbers only.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose: (1) emphasize published evaluation criteria and guide reviewers toward an appropriate overall score; (2) provide the applicant, Programmatic Panel and CDMRP with an informed measure of strengths/weaknesses. Evaluation-criteria scores were not averaged or mathematically manipulated to connect them to global or percentile scores.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall score (1.0–5.0 in 0.1 increments) and adjectival equivalents
rubrics_metrics.description: To obtain an overall score, panel members used a range of 1.0 to 5.0 (1.0 representing the highest merit and 5.0 the lowest), with scoring permitted in 0.1 increments. The OCRP averaged the panel member scores and rounded them to arrive at a two-digit number that corresponds to adjectival equivalents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adjectival equivalents used to guide reviewers: Outstanding (1.0–1.5), Excellent (1.6–2.0), Good (2.1–2.5), Fair (2.6–3.5) and Deficient (3.6–5.0). Overall scores are the average of panel member overall ratings, rounded to two digits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Summary Statement content and availability
rubrics_metrics.description: The Scientific Review Officer prepares a Summary Statement reporting peer review results for each application, including the evaluation criteria and overall scores, peer reviewers’ written comments, and the essence of panel discussions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Summary Statements are used by OCRP staff to report peer review results to the Programmatic Panel and, in accordance with DHA R&D-MRDC policy, are available to each applicant after completion of the review process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Programmatic review criteria and decision factors
rubrics_metrics.description: Programmatic review is a comparison-based process that considers scientific evaluations across all disciplines; the programmatic review criteria published in the PAs were: ratings and evaluations of the scientific peer review panels, programmatic relevance, relative impact, program portfolio balance and composition, and adherence to the intent of the award mechanism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Programmatic Panel members (diverse basic/clinical scientists and consumer advocates) do not automatically recommend funding based solely on high peer-review scores; they examine eligible applications in the context of limited funds, portfolio balance, and programmatic priorities. After programmatic recommendations, applications are routed to a designated official for final review and approval.
